messages:
Mei: Heads up — new onboarding report: Python streaming example can hang on Windows when cancelling the iterator.

Dan: ack. minimal repro?

Mei: run `examples/streaming_demo.py` on Win10, start generator, call `gen.close()` from another thread after first chunk. app prints chunk then never exits.

Lucia: logs?

Mei: snippet: `DEBUG chunk: {"text":"hi"}` then `DEBUG cancel requested` and process stays alive; socket left ESTABLISHED.

Dan: probably our blocking recv loop not being interrupted by generator finalizer on Windows. Linux unwinds fine.

Lucia: short fix: update sample to use `with client.stream(...) as s:` so context manager calls close on exit. Also add note in onboarding docs.

Mei: I'll PR the sample and doc change. long-term we should expose a StreamHandle with `close()/aclose()` and use `weakref.finalize` as a safety net.

Dan: also add typing overloads so `stream()` shows as `ContextManager[Iterator[str]]` and `AsyncContextManager[AsyncIterator[str]]` for better editor hints.

Lucia: add an e2e test that cancels after first chunk and asserts process exits within 1s on CI; mark Windows as xfail for now.

test-bot: build/523 started · ubuntu-latest · python 3.11

Mei: PR opened with sample+test. CI green on linux, windows runner flaky. I'll follow up with transport-level shutdown helper in a second PR.

Dan: thanks — nice triage.

Lucia: please include the onboarding note, that prevented this from hitting more new hires.
